highlights.title: New Home Statistics Range setting
changes: A new Home Statistics Range setting lets you pick Today, Last 24 Hours, Last 7 Days, Last Month, or Last 3 Months for.
The home stats panel updates its numbers and labels to reflect the chosen time span.
Tapping the home stats panel opens the full Statistics view on the same selected span.
Short spans (Today, Last 24 Hours) use the chart's in-memory data; longer spans fetch older readings in the background,.
Background refreshes for longer spans are throttled so updates occur at most once every 5 minutes.

highlights.title: Avoid startup overwrite of restored pump state
changes: Trio now saves a restored pump's state on the pump's processing (background) queue during startup.
This prevents a timing issue where an older snapshot could overwrite a newer pump state at launch.
Legacy saved pump data is cleared only after the new pump state is written to storage.

includedPullRequests.title: Add a Statistics Range setting for the home stats panel
includedPullRequests.body: Add a new setting, Features > User Interface > Statistics Range, to control whether the home stats panel shows data for today (current default), the last 24 hours, the last 7 days, the last month or the last 3 months. - The Time in Range, Distribution Bar and Averages faces compute over the chosen span, and their wording follows it ("Time in Range last 7 days", "Average of the Last 7 Days"). The Averages option drops "Today's". - Today and the last 24 hours still come from the chart's in-memory 72 h of glucose. Longer spans fetch readings on a background context; a new refresh cancels the previous one, and refreshes driven by new readings are throttled to one every 5 minutes. - Start dates use the same calendar arithmetic as the Statistics screen's glucose fetches, and the Statistics screen now opens on the same span, so tapping the panel shows matching numbers.

The pumpManager didSet attached the delegate and its queue, then wrote rawPumpManager from the calling thread. A pump manager that replays its state once the delegate queue is set (TandemKit does) runs pumpManagerDidUpdateState on processQueue at the same moment, which also writes rawPumpManager. includedPullRequests.title: Add Glycemia Risk Index feature with calculations and UI components
Add Glycemia Risk Index feature with calculations and UI components
Fix glucose color for mmol/L in comma-decimal locales
includedPullRequests.body:
The Live Activity and the contact image picked the glucose color by parsing the formatted reading with Decimal(string:). In regions that use a comma as decimal separator "4,8" is parsed as 4, so with mmol/L a 4.8 reading and a 4.4 low threshold showed red on the lock screen and contact image, and orange instead of yellow-green with the dynamic color scheme.

The Live Activity state now includes the reading in mg/dL, and the lock screen and Dynamic Island use one shared color helper that compares reading, thresholds and target in mg/dL, same as the main app and the Live Activity chart. This also removes a unit mismatch in the Dynamic Island, where mmol readings were compared against mg/dL thresholds with the static scheme. That one wasn't visible because the island draws the reading in the primary color with the static scheme. The contact image now uses the numeric reading too.

The expired "--" Live Activity state is now colored as in range for mmol users as well. Before, it was colored as high for mmol users and in range for mg/dL users.
